newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Aug 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Aug 19.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- The chief of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Joseph Yam said that the Hong Kong dollar speculation had been defeated, and warned that banks would be punished if found assisting speculators.

-- Some people compared the chief of the provisional legislature Rita Fan to the imperious and tyrant Jiang Qing, wife of the late Chinese Chairman Mao Zedong. But Fan said it was just a personal attack from holders of different opinions.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Regional analysts said that the Hong Kong dollar peg faced a challenge this week from international hedge funds emboldened by their string of triumphs around the region.
--At least 14 mainland-funded companies were aiming to tap the Hong Kong stock market for more than $30 billion over the next four months to capitalise on growing confidence in the mainland economy.
--HONG KONG STANDARD -- Shanghai had moved a step closer to becoming China's centre for international shipping with the establishment of the China Shipping Group.

-- EXPRESS NEWS -- Six groups protested against the absence of government officials from yesterday's commemorations of the end of the Sino-Japanese War. Some academics said that the incident showed that the Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa lacked political skills.

-- TA KUNG PAO -- China would adjust its overall arrangement of cities. In the next 15 years, the proportion of cities would be brought up from 26 per cent to 42 per cent. Plans had been drawn out to upgrade cities and speed up modernisation.
--SING TAO -- China's total state-owned assets had reached 6,500 billion yuan at the end of last year, representing a steady increase of 15 per cent from 1995 Newsroom (852) 28436441
